theory: Harness instructions are named templates rendered under strict missing-variable rules and identified as explicit prompt sets. User slash templates are input expansion, not silently part of the harness instruction identity.
instead_of: Embedding prompt prose across Python call sites would make text changes difficult to review and make recorded prompt identity incomplete.

absorption.rationale: More templates fit naturally; backend-specific exact instruction identity still needs a richer recorded contract.

world_mapping.rationale: Named harness instructions and user-provided text have distinct experimental roles.

abstraction.rationale: Jinja strict rendering and one package loader avoid reimplemented formatting at call sites.

justification.rationale: Prompt-set membership is justified separately for staged, batch and user templates.

honest_limits.rationale: The payload documents a conservative Codex schema-template asymmetry instead of claiming exact backend equivalence.

rehearsals.requirement: Add a required field to the proof prompt
rehearsals.why: Strict rendering fails any caller that omits it.

rehearsals.requirement: Record exactly which structure instruction each backend received
rehearsals.why: The existing payload explicitly includes a structure template the Codex SDK path does not append.

rehearsals.requirement: Add a reusable user slash template
rehearsals.why: User templates are a separate input-expansion layer.
